newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurostocks at lows on Dow drop,dlr pressured.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurostocks at lows on Dow drop,dlr pressured.

text.p: European equity markets fell on Wednesday morning, hit by a large overnight decline on Wall Street to hover around session lows by midday.

On currency markets, the dollar was also an early loser after a hawkish assessment on German inflation from the Bundesbank appeared to increase the chances of higher German interest rates and boosted the mark across the board.
In the morning session, London dealers took a relaxed view of Wall Street's decline, which saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average lose 101.27 points to 7960.84.
The FTSE-100 index of leading shares was some 25 points lower initially after finishing at its second highest ever level on Tuesday at 5075.8.
"The (London) market is not immune but it is used to these big swings on Wall St," said Charterhouse group economist Richard Jeffrey.

Dealers were less sanguine, however, about the latest British unemployment data, published an hour after the market opened. July figures showed an unexpectedly low jobless rate of 5.5 percent, down from 5.7 percent in June.
This was a larger fall than the market had bargained for, and by 1200 GMT the FTSE-100 decline had steepened, showing a loss of 48.0 points, a 0.95 percent fall, to 5027.8.
The Bank of England's August inflation report, released later, signalled that monetary policy may stay on hold after four successive monthly rate rises.

"The Monetary Policy Committee concluded that monetary policy has now reached a position at which it should be possible to pause in order to assess the direction in which the risks (to inflation) are likely to materialise," the central bank said.
The report itself had little impact on the pound, but the mark's new-found strength pushed sterling lower and by midday it was at 2.9116/26 marks against a close in Europe on Tuesday of 2.9485 marks.

The Frankfurt bourse also lost ground, with the DAX index falling 1.68 percent by midday to 4,289.31. Dealers said sentiment was undermined by the failure of the Dow Jones to close above the psychologically important 8,000 point level.

Monday's Wall Street drop was not the only negative U.S. influence on European stocks. Nervousness surrounding U.S. July producer price and retail sales data due at 1230 GMT also made dealers edgy about any possible inflationary signs.

French dealers were particularly anxious about the upcoming U.S. numbers, which are expected to show a 0.1 percent rise in the producer price index and 0.7 percent rise in retail sales. The CAC-40 index was 73.46 points, or 2.45 percent, lower at 2,925.24 by 1116 GMT.
By midday, the dollar was at session lows at 1.8453/58 marks after the warning on inflation from Germany's Bundesbank boosted the mark across the board.

"There has been a general move into marks this morning after the Bundesbank report," said Mark Geddes, treasury economist at ABN AMRO in London. "The report showed that the Bundesbank is concerned about inflation and that has increased speculation about a German rate rise."

In its August monthly report, published early on Wednesday, the Bundesbank said it could not overlook a stronger rise in consumer prices in the last few months, and would shape its policy in such a way that price stability can be maintained.

"The assertion that the exchange rate is very significant in policy decisions, the fact that they highlight the recent rise in some inflation figures and the desire to see M3 growth lower, suggest they may be closer to a rate increase than previously thought," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank of America in London.
On Tuesday, data for July showed that German inflation rose to 1.9 percent, the highest level since June 1995 and up from 1.7 percent in June.

Even though the CPI data was boosted by one-off factors last month, economists expect it to rise above 2.0 percent soon, the level regarded as acceptable by the Bundesbank. German import prices, due to be released later this month, are also key for signs whether the weakness of the mark is boosting inflation.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted around 1.8513/19 marks and 116.39 yen, compared with 1.8665 and 115.78 in late trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1125 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 56.0 points at 5,019.9.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was down 80.58 points at 4282.82.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was down 70.90 at 2927.67.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was $2.45 an ounce firmer in London at $328.60. Silver was up four cents at $4.47.
